## D7 at a glance

- **The gate:** top-decile capture {{< var ews.capture >}} of deteriorations on the held-out
  {{< var ews.test_share >}} of the booked book, against a gate of
  {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}} (lift {{< var ews.lift >}}×); PR-AUC
  {{< var ews.pr_auc >}} against a base rate of {{< var ews.base_rate >}}. Both met, the
  capture gate narrowly: {{< var ews.boot.capture_below_gate >}} of bootstrap resamples fall
  below it ([7.5](performance.qmd)).
- **AUC is reported, not gated:** held-out AUC {{< var ews.auc >}}, indistinguishable from the
  {{< var ceiling.ews.oracle_model.auc >}} a reference LightGBM, configured as the committed one
  and given every observable column, reaches on the same rows; even the generator's noise-free
  logit reaches only {{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}} there. The data's noise caps AUC; capture is what the review workflow
  uses, so capture is what is gated ([7.9](gate.qmd)).
- **Quote the held-out number:** over the whole book the same model shows capture
  {{< var ews.whole.capture >}} and AUC {{< var ews.whole.auc >}}, but most of the book is
  the model's own training rows. That figure, and the module's default watchlist of
  {{< var ews.watchlist.n >}} (the portal serves the top {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n >}} of
  the same ranking; the v1 page shows {{< var ews.watchlist.page.n >}}), are in-sample
  (finding 2, [7.7](limitations.qmd)).
- **The tiers do not hold their mix on new accounts:** the cutoffs are quantiles of in-sample
  probabilities, so the High tier, {{< var ews.tier.High.share >}} of the book by construction,
  holds {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.share >}} of held-out accounts (finding 1).
- **No better than the score alone on AUC:** the paired interval for the difference,
  {{< var ews.pd_score.diff_lo >}} to {{< var ews.pd_score.diff_hi >}}, contains zero
  ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-benchmark)).
- **Lead time is unmeasured:** the label is drawn over the same months as the features,
  so how far ahead the model warns has not been tested (finding 8).
- **Eight open findings** the chapter raises about its own model, tiers and triggers
  ([7.7](limitations.qmd)).
:::

Early Warning watches the loans the bank has already booked and asks which of them are
likely to deteriorate in the months ahead ([7.1](purpose.qmd)). It is three things served
together: a gradient-boosted model (LightGBM) on {{< var ews.n_features >}} features built
from each account's monthly history, its origination file and the Business Credit Score's
own output ([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd)); **risk tiers** cut from the model's probability;
and **named triggers**, fixed rules on the behavioural features that give a reviewer a reason
([7.3](methodology.qmd)). It prioritises booked loans for human review and changes no credit
decision by itself, which makes it Tier 2 ([D0](../d0-summary.qmd#risk-tiering)).

{{< include ../../_generated/ews-headline.md >}}

Measured on the held-out {{< var ews.test_share >}} of the {{< var ews.n_book >}} booked
accounts: {{< var ews.n_test >}} accounts the model never saw while it was fitted, redrawn
exactly as `ews/src/train.py` drew them ([7.2](data.qmd#ews-split)). Every number in the
chapter is a named fact, recomputed through the module's own functions — the saved model on
`compute_ews_features`, `risk_tier`, `flag_triggers` and `watchlist` — by `python verify.py`;
the [fact index](../../reference/facts.qmd) gives each one's source and population. The
chapter documents the model, tiers and triggers as committed: it changes none of them.
